findings: The selected x86_64 callback C ABI void(unsigned long, void*) matches unsafe extern C fn(CULong,*mut c_void), with CULong=u64; both exported Rust names have exactly one no_mangle definition in the proposed module. Both leaf functions perform precisely one direct call to the existing selected lock_helpers writer noirq counterpart, forwarding lock_addr and node unchanged. The cast preserves the live lock address and introduces no reference, allocation, retained pointer, node dereference, IRQ save/restore, or alternate lock algorithm.

The selected x86 SPINLOCK_IN_MCS_RWLOCK header and existing Rust layout agree on the 64-byte aligned lock with slock at offset zero. Both old C and existing Rust noirq writer functions ignore the caller node and operate on slock. The Rust spinlock functions retain preempt_disable before acquisition, existing atomic ordering, and preempt_enable after unlock; this leaf does not change them.

Unchanged ptrace_report_clone owns distinct lock and updatelock stack nodes and passes both through a synchronous Rust-body call. The existing body validates callback/node presence before acquisition, performs lock(update_lock,lock_node)/unlock of the same pair, and conditionally lock(new_update_lock,new_lock_node)/unlock of the same pair, without returning between a successful acquisition and matching release. No callback or node escapes from this leaf; no new lifetime or alias requirement is introduced.

C and Rust selection are paired within the existing Linux6.12 x86_64 non-UBSAN cohort; the explicit Rust source dependency and cfg module are added together. The patch does not modify the parent C body or Rust body, registry, existing lock functions, callback order or oracle.
